items: Agnes Callamard, Amnesty International's secretary general, warned that US sanctions against the ICC could put at risk its operations and the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte.
Callamard emphasized that if the ICC cannot function due to these sanctions, it risks losing its credibility and independence.

MANILA, Philippines – Amnesty International secretary general and human rights activist Agnes Callamard warned that the United States’ sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) could imperil the court’s operations, including the case of former president Rodrigo Duterte.

At the sidelines of the event, the Amnesty secretary general told Palawan News that these sanctions could cause the collapse of the court. “If the ICC is unable to function, the ICC will collapse. Or the trial will deliver the verdict that will have lost its credibility. At all levels, whether it’s operational or political, it’s bad news.”

Callamard was in the Philippines for Rappler’s Social Good Summit on Saturday, November 20, where she and other advocates talked about the need to build a community amid threats of Artificial Intelligence. As United Nations Special Rapporteur on Extrajudicial Killings, she was barred by the Duterte administration from entering the country. The Marcos government lifted this ban only last September.

Callamard told Rappler, “The trial of ex-president Duterte is due to start on 30 November. It could take one year or probably more until judgment. If no action is taken to protect the ICC against the US sanctions, the trial may never proceed.”

In an interview with Rappler, Callamard said: “I was told that just this week, in a meeting of the state parties to the ICC, the diplomats of the most powerful countries, including Canada and the UK, and other G7 states, have insisted the only way forward is to negotiate with the US and agree to their demands. They continue to refuse to protect the ICC.”
According to Callamard, the US is giving the ICC until April to comply with the following:

items: No ICC jurisdiction over non-state parties or “an impunity carve-out for the USA”
Dropping of ICC investigations and arrest warrants in the Palestine situation

blocks.text: The Amnesty secretary general said that if the powerful countries that are part of the ICC “are prepared to negotiate with the US, the ICC will lose its independence and credibility.”

“The failure to protect the ICC is a betrayal of the mothers and fathers, sons and daughters of the Philippines that have spoken up against Duterte’s senseless war, against threats and intimidation,” she added.

Duterte has been detained in The Hague, Netherlands since March 2025 after he was arrested due to three counts of crimes against humanity case. His case stemmed from the alleged killings of the Davao Death Squad and his bloody war on drugs that killed nearly 30,000 people, according to several human rights organizations.
In April, the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I confirmed all three charges against the former president. His trial will start on November 30 at the ICC Trial Chamber III.

blocks.caption: ICC wraps up pre-trial hearings as Duterte’s November 30 case nears

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump, in the last years, has been pushing to sanction the ICC which has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and crimes of aggression.

In February 2025, Trump authorized economic and travel sanctions against those involved in the ICC probe into US citizens or allies like Israel. He imposed sanctions, in the same year, against four ICC judges over the issuance of an arrest warrant for Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu and a past decision to open a case into alleged war crimes by US troops in Afghanistan.

Just last August, the US government imposed sanctions against ICC President Tomoko Akane and Abdoulaye Seye, a senior ICC trial lawyer. But the most concerning development is the ICC-wide sanctions that the Trump administration is planning to announce soon.

Entity-wide sanctions would bar US citizens and companies from giving the ICC funds, goods, or services without permission from the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control. This would be tricky because banks often comply with these sanctions since they are dependent on access to the American financial system, according to Reuters.
Apart from this, ICC-wide sanctions could affect the court’s IT services and insurance, investigations, and payments to employees.

blocks.caption: Trump administration prepares sanctions vs ICC, sources say

blocks.text: Callamard urged European governments to “use their ‘blocking’ law, which bars European companies from complying with foreign sanctions. She also called on central banks in Europe to give the court bank accounts,” Palawan News reported.

She told Rappler: “There is only one response to the USA threats and sanctions: it must be protecting the ICC. Not appeasing the predator. They continue to refuse to protect the ICC. They are betraying decades of efforts forged in blood and tears to ensure that no one, absolutely no one should be above the law.” – Rappler.com
